candidates.summary: render's precondition is len(plan.Realms) > 0 but the guard above it, Plan.Empty, answers on plan.Gnoweb: a gnoweb plan with no realms reaches urlOf(plan.Realms[0]) and panics
candidates.failure_scenario: A pull request touches gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ (or contribs/gnodev/) in a tree where none of the four gnowebSeedRealms resolve under examples/gno.land -- one of them renamed or moved by that same PR, or a checkout that does not carry them. BuildPlan sets Gnoweb=true and leaves Realms empty, so Plan.Empty (!Gnoweb && len(Realms)==0) is false and the workflow's own gate, jq '.gnoweb or (.realms | length > 0)', passes too. render prints 'rendering 0 realm(s):', starts gnodev with no package dirs, then evaluates urlOf(plan.Realms[0]) for the readiness probe and panics with 'index out of range [0] with length 0'. The job dies on a Go stack trace with no preview and no comment, and the 'Show the gnodev log' step has nothing to show because gnodev never failed. The deeper form is Empty() reporting on what render consumes, len(p.Realms) == 0, since a plan with no realms renders nothing whatever set Gnoweb to true.

candidates.evidence: Both tests PASS at ecf7af0f2 with go1.25.9. TestGnowebPlanWithNoRealmsIsNotEmpty: BuildPlan returns gnoweb=true, realms=[], Empty()==false. TestRenderPanicsOnGnowebPlanWithNoRealms, with /bin/true standing in for gnodev: 'rendering 0 realm(s): ' then 'render panicked: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0'.

candidates.summary: startGnodev(cfg, root, dirs, port, logName) takes root and port as parameters while receiving a cfg that already carries both fields, and during the base pass those fields hold the head's values: 5 parameters become 3, same line count
candidates.failure_scenario: renderBase calls startGnodev(cfg, cfg.baseRoot, dirs, cfg.port+1, ...), so inside the callee cfg.root is the head checkout and cfg.port is the head's web port while the pass being started is the base one. Today the body happens to read only cfg.out and cfg.gnodev off the struct, so nothing is wrong; the next line added there that reaches for cfg.root or cfg.port -- the obvious spelling -- silently boots the base pass against the head tree or collides on the head's ports, and no test would see it because the base pass is best-effort and its failure only costs the comment an image. The deeper form is one source for each value: the caller copies cfg and sets cfg.root, cfg.port = cfg.baseRoot, cfg.port+1 before the call.

candidates.summary: the command name is validated after findRoot, readLines and BuildPlan have run, so a typo walks examples/ and blocks on stdin instead of printing the usage line run() already holds
candidates.failure_scenario: `gnopreview help` (or any misspelling of plan/render) parses flags, finds the root, then reads -changed, which defaults to '-'. With a terminal or an open pipe on stdin the process hangs forever and never reaches 'unknown command'; redirected from a file it walks every package under examples/gno.land and parses their imports first. Moving the switch above the work -- a three-line guard after 'cmd, args := args[0], args[1:]' -- makes the usage error immediate and costs nothing else.

candidates.summary: `if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil { return err }` cannot run: the flag set is built with flag.ExitOnError, so Parse exits the process on a bad flag
candidates.failure_scenario: No failure; three lines of dead error handling sit in a run() whose whole shape exists to funnel errors through main's single Fprintln/os.Exit(1). A reader takes the branch as proof that a bad flag is reported the same way, and it is not: `gnopreview plan -bogus` prints the flag package's own usage and exits 2 without ever returning to run. Either drop the branch or switch the flag set to flag.ContinueOnError, which is the depth the surrounding code is written at.
candidates.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && go build -o /tmp/gnopreview . && /tmp/gnopreview plan -bogus; echo $?
candidates.evidence: exit 2, output is flag's usage dump ('  -timeout duration ... (default 5m0s)'), never main's 'gnopreview: ' prefix, which is what a returned error would have printed with exit 1.

candidates.summary: readLines reads stdin as the file "/dev/stdin" where io.ReadAll(os.Stdin) is the same length and does not depend on a device node existing
candidates.failure_scenario: The default -changed value is '-', so the stdin branch is the one a local run takes. os.ReadFile("/dev/stdin") needs /dev/stdin to exist and to be readable: it is absent on Windows, and in a container built without a populated /dev the same invocation fails with 'open /dev/stdin: no such file or directory' rather than reading the pipe it was handed. The CI job passes -changed changed.txt, so nothing in the workflow exercises this path.
candidates.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && sed -i 's|os.ReadFile("/dev/stdin")|io.ReadAll(os.Stdin)|' main.go && goimports -w main.go && go test ./... && printf 'gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/x.go\n' | go run . plan -changed -
